proposal.name: Build again at xhigh when the loop guard stops a build

plan.name: Build again at xhigh when the loop guard stops a build
plan.summary: When the loop guard (D-0115) stops a build's first agent run, in a project's synthesis (synth.Synthesize) or a plumbing plan's build (plumbing.Builder.Build), the build runs the agent once more at a fallback effort, with the same job, workspace, transcript and limits, its timeout starting again, so it keeps any files it wrote; that second run's usage and error become the build's, and there's never a third run (D-0125). The effort comes from a new FallbackEffort string on synth.Options and plumbing.Builder, where empty never runs the agent again, and reaches the second run in a new synth.Job.Effort, which ClaudeCode passes as --effort in place of its own; a first run's Effort is empty, so it thinks at the backend's own effort, and the build records the fallback in a new `Fallback *synth.Fallback` field, JSON "fallback", on synth.Result and plumbing.BuildResult, whose Effort is the second run's effort and whose Why is the first run's error. When the final gate can't run, Synthesize now returns its result, with no final report, and an error that leads with the agent's run's error, wrapped, when the run failed, so a build whose agent looped says it looped, not only that the gate found no Go files, as #91's did. The factory's posts and pull request bodies for both kinds of build, passing or failing, and synth.Summary say when a build fell back, to which effort, and why, quoting the first run's error; drafts, plans, plans of issues and reviews never run again; and `watch` and `synthesize` take -fallback-effort, xhigh by default, which must be empty or an effort and reaches their builds only when it's below -effort, so at the default max a build falls back to xhigh. SPEC.md says so, citing D-0125, and since this changes the trusted base, a person merges it.

tests.name: TestASynthesisThatLoopsAtMaxRunsAgainAtXhigh
tests.says: With a stand-in agent whose replies at max are only thinking, cut off at the output limit, after it wrote one file, and which writes the code at xhigh, a synthesis runs it twice, at max and then at xhigh, in the same workspace with the first run's file still there; both files reach the result, the run's outcome is the second's success, and the result says it fell back to xhigh because of the guard's reason.

tests.name: TestASynthesisThatLoopsAtXhighTooFailsWithTheGuardsReason
tests.says: A synthesis whose stand-in agent loops at xhigh too, and writes nothing, as #91's did, runs it exactly twice, and fails with an error that is the guard's and says so, even though the final gate then found nothing to check, and its result says it fell back to xhigh.

tests.name: TestAFallbackRunTellsClaudeCodeItsEffort
tests.says: Claude Code set to max is told --effort xhigh, once, for a job whose effort is xhigh, building or reviewing alike, and --effort max for a job that names none.

tests.name: TestAPlanBuildThatLoopsAtMaxPassesAtXhigh
tests.says: With a stand-in agent whose replies at max are only thinking, cut off at the output limit, after it began the plan's file, and which finishes it at xhigh, a plan's build runs it twice, at max and then at xhigh, in the same workspace with the file as the first run left it, and passes on the second run, with the finished file in the checkout; its result says it fell back to xhigh because of the guard's reason, and the review runs once, at max.

tests.name: TestAPlanBuildThatLoopsAtXhighTooFailsWithTheGuardsReason
tests.says: A plan's build whose stand-in agent loops at xhigh too runs it exactly twice and fails, its summary giving the guard's reason, and its result says it fell back to xhigh.

tests.name: TestADraftWhoseAgentLoopsIsntRunAgain
tests.says: A draft of statements, a plumbing plan and a PRD's plan of issues whose stand-in agent loops at max each run it exactly once, at max, and their problem gives the guard's reason.

tests.name: TestAPullRequestSaysItsBuildFellBack
tests.says: When a project's build or a plan's build fell back to xhigh and passed, the factory's pull request post and the pull request's body each say xhigh and give the guard's reason, from the build's saved record.

tests.name: TestAFailedBuildSaysItsAgentLooped
tests.says: When a project's build fell back and its agent looped at xhigh too, so the final gate couldn't run, as #91's did, and when a plan's build fell back and failed its tests, the factory's failure post says xhigh and gives the guard's reason.

usage.summary:
I've written the plan for #154, and the check passed on the first try: it holds together, and all 8 acceptance tests fail on the code as it is. When the loop guard stops a build's first agent run, whether a project's synthesis or a plumbing plan's, the build runs the agent once more at xhigh (`-fallback-effort`, empty turns it off) in the same workspace, and its result, pull request and posts say so and quote the guard's reason; drafts, plans and reviews never run again, and a build whose agent loops at xhigh too fails with the guard's reason instead of only "no Go files" as #91's did.

The check only shows the tests fail now, not that they'll pass once the change is made. They fail because they use fields that don't exist yet, and I couldn't run them, so I traced each path through the code by hand. A synthesis can't reach its final gate without Docker, so its tests check the second run, the kept files and the recorded fallback; "passes on its second run" is shown on the plumbing build, which uses a stand-in `docker`.

Decision for you before ratifying: the build doesn't know what effort the agent's first run used, so I made `watch` and `synthesize` pass `-fallback-effort` to builds only when it's lower than `-effort`. At the default max, builds fall back to xhigh; at `-effort xhigh` or lower they don't fall back at all unless you set a lower fallback. The change touches the trusted base, so a person merges it.
